rationale: This record is an Editorial Foreword introducing journal articles on general bureaucratic anxieties in colonial history, such as British East India Company recordkeeping/forgery in Madras and racialized police administration in early twentieth-century South Africa. It contains no household or community water or sanitation topic (C1 = no, C4 = no) and is an editorial foreword rather than primary empirical research or a systematic review (C3 = no). Primary exclusion code E01 (wrong topic).
plain_vs_narrow_note: Excluded under both readings. evidence_quotes.quote: Three of our authors take us on a global tour of bureaucracies in flux.
Bhavani Raman considers the bureaucratic anxieties fueled by pervasive mistrust between officials of the British East India Company in Madras, its native functionaries, and local populations.

Shear looks specifically at police forces, which relied heavily on whites even though this meant less familiarity with local populations, poorer intelligence, and limited ability to investigate crimes.
